blocks.text:
**Jaundice, pale stools, dark urine or itch:** not isolated — fractionated bilirubin and hepatology today.
**Vomiting blood, black stools or active bleeding:** emergency department now.
**Fever with jaundice or right upper quadrant pain:** think cholangitis or a stone — emergency department now (blood cultures, ultrasound).
**Fever or rash after a new antiepileptic drug:** think DRESS or drug-induced liver injury — same day.
**Bloody diarrhea, weight loss or poor growth:** think IBD — fecal calprotectin, pediatric GI this week.
**Large spleen or low platelets:** not isolated — possible advanced liver disease; hepatology within days.

items: Primary or autoimmune sclerosing cholangitis — IBD may be silent
Alagille syndrome — murmur, face, vertebrae, eyes
Valproate toxicity — check ALT, INR and ammonia
Drug-induced liver injury — once ALT or bilirubin rise

blocks.text:
GGT sits on the canalicular membrane and in bile duct cells, and also in kidney and pancreas — but not in bone. It is high in young infants and lowest at 1–6 years, below adult values (lesson 01-01), so it must be read against the range for age.

GGT is sensitive but not specific. Adult guidelines list alcohol, obesity and drugs as the usual causes of an isolated rise; ACG names phenytoin and barbiturates and advises against using GGT as a screen when other liver tests are normal. BSG still calls GGT one of the best predictors of liver mortality. In children, carbamazepine mainly raises GGT, by enzyme induction (Cepelak 1998): after a year GGT was raised in 34% of children on carbamazepine and 14.9% on valproate (Hadzagic-Catibusic 2017).

In children, the cause that matters most is bile duct disease. PSC is usually silent and lives beside IBD; ESPGHAN advises GGT checks every 3–6 months in every child with IBD, prompt investigation at ≥ 2 × ULN, further evaluation if a milder rise persists > 1 month, and MRCP to diagnose (van Rheenen 2025). In 469 children with IBD, 34 developed PSC; a GGT under 2 × ULN (100 U/L) had a negative predictive value of 98%, so MRCP could be skipped (Berhane 2025, single center). Once PSC is diagnosed, GGT also tracks prognosis: normal GGT at 1 year meant 91% versus 67% 5-year event-free survival (Deneau 2018, 287 children).

items.text: GGT is high in young infants but lowest at 1–6 years. A value "normal" for an adult can be raised in a toddler (lesson 01-01).
Well child on carbamazepine, phenytoin or phenobarbital with GGT alone up: likely enzyme induction. No workup unless GGT keeps rising or ALT or bilirubin rise (expert opinion).
Obese teen with "isolated" GGT: check ALT against 26 (boys) or 22 (girls) — if above, it is not isolated (AASLD 2025).
Every child with IBD: check GGT every 3–6 months. PSC is often found this way (van Rheenen 2025).
In IBD, GGT < 2 × ULN makes PSC unlikely enough to skip MRCP — but a rise lasting > 1 month still needs a cause workup, and GGT checks continue (Berhane 2025; van Rheenen 2025).
A normal ultrasound does not exclude sclerosing cholangitis. MRCP is the test (ACG 2017; van Rheenen 2025).

positions.kwo_2017_acg_lft: Do not use GGT to screen when other liver tests are normal
positions.bsg_2018_lft: Include GGT in the initial liver panel
positions.espghan_2025_psc_ibd: Regular GGT screening in every child with IBD

rows.note: The app does not order GGT alone to screen, except in IBD — where it finds silent PSC.

positions.kwo_2017_acg_lft: Alcohol; phenytoin, barbiturates; pancreatic, kidney disease, diabetes

rows.note: Adult lists. In children add bile duct disease (PSC, Alagille, choledochal cyst) and the newborn range.

rows.topic: When bile duct disease is suspected

positions.kwo_2017_acg_lft: MRCP or ERCP, as PSC may not show on ultrasound
positions.espghan_2025_psc_ibd: MRCP is the modality of choice; biopsy for small-duct PSC or AIH overlap

rows.topic: Mild GGT rise in IBD (< 2 × ULN)

positions.espghan_2025_psc_ibd: Persisting > 1 month: further evaluation; ≥ 2 × ULN: prompt investigation
positions.berhane_2025_ggt_ibd: < 2 × ULN (100 U/L): PSC very unlikely (NPV 98%); MRCP and biopsy can be omitted

rows.note: Compatible: the app works up a persistent mild rise but keeps MRCP for ≥ 2 × ULN or a rising GGT.
